title: Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter 3
language: Greek (Codex Sinaiticus) / English (J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers)
source: Codex Sinaiticus folio + transcription (codexsinaiticus.org) + J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891)
description: Epistle of Barnabas chapter 3. Manuscript page scan(s) from Codex Sinaiticus hosted by the Codex Sinaiticus Project, with the Project's verbatim transcription of the Greek and the English of J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891).
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio(s) of Codex Sinaiticus containing this chapter, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Each section links to the specific folio holding its verses.
  2. Original text: The Codex Sinaiticus Project's verbatim transcription of the folio shown (uncial letters, lunate sigma, nomina sacra preserved).
  3. English translation: J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891), public domain, retrieved verbatim from Lightfoot 1891 via earlychristianwritings.com transcription.

Why this is here: Codex Sinaiticus binds this text after Revelation, alongside the canonical books. Reading it on the same parchment as the Gospels is primary evidence for how a 4th-century Christian community treated it.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>λεγει ουν παλιν περι τουτων προϲ αυτουϲ ϊνα τι μοι νηϲτευεται λεγει κϲ ωϲ ϲημερον ακουϲθηναι κραυγη την φωνην υμων ου ταυτην την νηϲτια εγω εξελεξαμην λεγει κϲ ουκ ανθρωπον ταπινουντα την ψυχην αυτου <sup>2</sup>ουδ αν καμψηται ωϲ κρικον τον τραχηλον ϋμων και ϲακκον και ϲποδον ϋποϲτρωϲηται ουδ ουτωϲ καλεϲεται νηϲτιαν δεκτην <sup>3</sup>προϲ ημαϲ λεγει ϊδου αυτη νηϲτια ην εγω εξελεξαμην λεγει κϲ ουκ ανθρωπον ταπινουντα την ψυχην αυτου αλλα λυε παν ϲυνδεϲμον αδικιαϲ διαλυε ϲτραγγαλιαϲ βιαιων ϲυναλλαγματων αποϲτελλε τεθραυϲμενουϲ εν αφεϲει και παϲαν αδικον ϲυνγραφη διαϲπα διαθρυπτε πινωϲιν το αρτον ϲου · και γυμνον εαν ειδηϲ περιβαλε αϲτεγουϲ ειϲαγε ειϲ τον οικον ϲου · και εαν ιδηϲ ταπινον ουχ υπεροψη αυτον ουδε απο των οικιων του ϲπερματοϲ ϲου <sup>4</sup>τοτε ραγηϲεται προϊμον το φωϲ ϲου και τα ιματα ϲου ταχεωϲ ανατελει και προπορευϲεται εμπροϲθεν ϲου η δικαιοϲυνη και η δοξα του θυ περιϲτελει ϲε <sup>5</sup>και βοηϲειϲ και ο θϲ επακουϲεται ϲου ετι λαλουντοϲ ϲου ερι ιδου παρειμι εαν αφεληϲ απο ϲου ϲυνδεϲμον και χειροτονιαν και ρημα γογγυϲμου και δωϲ πινωντι τον αρτον ϲου εκ ψυχηϲ ϲου και ψυχη τεταπινωμενην ελαιηϲειϲ
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>He speaketh again therefore to them concerning these things; Wherefore fast ye for Me, saith the Lord, so that your voice is heard this day crying aloud? This is not the fast which have chosen, saith the Lord; not a man abasing his soul; <sup>2</sup>not though ye should bend your neck as a hoop, and put on sackcloth and make your bed of ashes, not even so shall ye call a fast that is acceptable. <sup>3</sup>But unto us He saith; Behold, this is the fast which I have chosen, saith the Lord; loosen every band of wickedness, untie the tightened cords of forcible contracts, send away the broken ones released and tear in pieces every unjust bond. Break thy bread to the hungry, and if thou seest one naked clothe him; bring the shelterless into thy house, and if thou seest a humble man, thou shalt not despise him, neither shall any one of thy household and of thine own seed. <sup>4</sup>Then shall thy light break forth in the morning, and thy healing shall arise quickly, and righteousness shall go forth before thy face, and the glory of God shall environ thee. <sup>5</sup>Then shalt thou cry out and God shall hear thee; while thou art still speaking, He shall say 'Lo, I am here'; if thou shalt take away from thee the yoke and the stretching forth of the finger and the word of murmuring, and shalt give thy bread to the hungry heartily, and shalt pity the abased soul.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>ειϲ τουτο ουν αδελφοι μακροθυμοϲ προβλεψαϲ ωϲ εν ακερεοϲυνη πιϲτευϲει ο λαοϲ ον ητοιμαϲεν εν τω ηγαπημενω αυτου προεφανερωϲεν γαρ ημιν περι παντων εινα μη προϲρηϲϲωμεθα ωϲ επιλυτοι τω εκινων νομων
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>To this end therefore, my brethren, He that is long-suffering, foreseeing that the people whom He had prepared in His well-beloved would believe in simplicity, manifested to us beforehand concerning all things, that we might not as novices shipwreck ourselves upon their law.

verification.translator: J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891)
